title: NEW! Minneapolis snowstorm recap
description: All videos were from the Twin Cities during a 1-3" snow fall on Tuesday, Dec 7, 2021.

transcript.text: We've got over two dozen incidents to show you in under five minutes. These are going to count you fast in hopes that we all remember to slow down. Stay with us to the end because we've got one incident involving a school bus plus a pile up caught on camera. And this all happened today in the Twin Cities in Minnesota. Be informed, be safe, and keep watching. We've been tracking the situation all day over 400 crashes in Minnesota on an inch or two of snow. It's still early in the winter season, so drivers are trying to remember how to do. drive in the winter, plus temperatures today were pretty cold, around 7 degrees Fahrenheit, which made salt less effective in preventing icy roadways. There are some key learnings from these videos, but the biggest takeaway is to drive with some humility and slow down. And I'll be honest with you, I volunteer to help create these videos, and somewhere inside of me is a desire to speed, go fast, maybe have a little fun when I drive, but then every day I see these crashes, and every day it's a reminder to be a little safer 10% safer 20% safer you don't have to be paranoid we're not asking for people to become priestly drivers but just five or 10 miles per hour slower it adds up and I think these videos are going to show that it's better to arrive late than to arrive sorry and you don't want to be stuck on the side of the road feeling embarrassed and being featured in one of our videos if you're not driving with just a little bit of humility and this is in my experience, an inch of snow can make you humble real fast. A special shout out to Mendot, Minnesota Department of Transportation, which by our account now operates more than 900 cameras across Minnesota and hands down has one of the best and most sophisticated operations in the country, bar none. These incidents happen all over the country, but Minnesota has some of the best visibility and transparency to traffic incidents. You won't see educational, real life, day traffic safety information like this anywhere else not anywhere in the United States not anywhere in the world is bringing you real-time traffic summaries like this now as you're watching these videos again all from the last 24 hours think about your own potential to be involved in a crash what would you do after a crash most public safety agencies recommend that you stay in your vehicle with your seatbelt on if needing to be out of the vehicle limit your time outside and try to keep a guardrail or concrete barrier between you and traffic. Just think chances of survival for a car hitting a pedestrian with speeds above 58 miles per hour are only 10%. Survivors and medics that we've talked to also recommend being extremely careful with your spine and your neck after a crash. You might have whiplash, a spinal injury, or a traumatic brain injury. Unless there are overriding concerns like your car being on fire, it might be good. to wait for professionals to safely help you out of your car in a crash if no one is injured and it's safe to do so try to get your car out of the lane of traffic this will likely help keep you and your car a little bit safer and more intact it'll help traffic flow a little bit better but it'll also decrease the chance of a secondary collision if your car's not drivable or you're injured don't worry about this too much it's just something to keep in mind if possible we just showed you a ton of incidents all from Minneapolis and St. Paul all from one day, December 7th, from one to two inches of snow. Now we've got some big incidents that happened, the first being on Highway 61 in the southeast metro involving the school bus. Thankfully we're not aware of any serious injuries, but multiple crashes over just a half mile of highway. Then in the evening commute, a multi-car pile up I-494 and Highway 61 in Newport, Minnesota, also a southeast Metro community. This is definitely a situation where you should stay in your car or drive to a safe location further down the road. Don't worry about getting out and exchanging info in the middle of a pile up. Like, subscribe, and share. Stay informed. We don't waste a minute of your time.
